key_insight: DOPD introduces dual on-policy distillation, a training strategy that uses both teacher-side and student-side privileged information to create stronger supervision while avoiding the misleading “privilege illusion” that can distort evaluation of distillation gains.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of getting high-quality supervision for on-policy distillation without confusing true student capability transfer with gains that come only from extra privileged inputs to the teacher or student.
method: Uses on-policy distillation, supervising student-sampled trajectories with dense token-level signals.
Infuses privileged information into both teacher and student in a controlled way to improve supervision quality.
Introduces the notion of privilege illusion and designs the approach to separate real transfer gains from superficial improvements caused by privileged inputs.
impact: This matters because it can help practitioners distill stronger models more reliably, especially when standard distillation underestimates or misattributes performance. The method provides a clearer path to transferring capabilities in sequence generation and other token-level tasks.
visual_elements: A side-by-side pipeline showing standard distillation vs. dual on-policy distillation.
An illustration of teacher and student trajectories with token-level supervision signals.
A diagram highlighting 'privileged information' and the 'privilege illusion' failure mode.

paper_authors: Xinlei Yu, Gen Li, Qingyi Si, Guibin Zhang, Yuqi Xu
